summary: Gallium oxide thin films were deposited by plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition (PEALD) using trimethylgallium (TMGa) as the gallium precursor and oxygen (O2) plasma as the oxidant. The films were characterized for their optical and electrical properties, showing excellent performance even at low temperatures. The study aimed to explore the feasibility of low-temperature growth of Ga2O3 films for electronic and optoelectronic applications.
evidence: Gallium oxide (Ga2O3) thin films were deposited by plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition (PEALD) applying a capacitively coupled plasma source where trimethylgallium (TMGa) as the gallium precursor and oxygen (O2) plasma were used in a substrate temperature (Ts) in range of 80 –200 °C. The PEALD process delivered a constant growth rate in the investigated substrate temperature range; the grown thin Ga2O3 films exhibited an ideal gallium to oxygen (Ga:O) ratio with lowest carbon contamination for films prepared at 150 °C. Furthermore, the films show excellent optical and electrical properties exhibiting values close to the ones of bulk crystalline material.
